requirement: Describe TIGER as a prospective open-label randomized two-arm parallel trial conducted in Stockholm emergency medical services, comparing guideline-based care plus prehospital point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin I testing with guideline-based care alone.
acceptable_values: hs-TnI plus usual care versus usual care

evidence.text: The protocol defines the open randomized parallel design and the intervention and control conditions.

requirement: Specify 2:1 electronic randomization in REDCap after informed consent during the prehospital-care phase, allocating approximately 946 participants to hs-TnI plus guideline care and 473 to guideline care alone.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the 2:1 REDCap allocation process and planned arm totals.

requirement: Before finalization, state how the REDCap sequence is generated and concealed and whether any blocking, site or ambulance-unit stratification is used; do not invent these details from the stated 2:1 ratio.

evidence.text: The protocol names REDCap and the 2:1 ratio but gives no sequence-generation, blocking, stratification or concealment details.

requirement: Define the randomized target population as consenting adults aged at least 18 years on a primary EMS assignment with chest pain or EMS clinical suspicion of myocardial infarction, excluding people without a valid Swedish personal identity number, without consent capacity, on a non-primary EMS assignment or classified as Level-1 trauma.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the randomized eligibility criteria.

requirement: Before finalization, reconcile the primary analysis population: the protocol says the trial uses an intention-to-treat approach among randomized suspected-MI patients, whereas the reference SAP restricts the study population to participants subsequently diagnosed with MI at discharge; define whether the confirmatory effect is estimated in all randomized participants, a discharge-confirmed-MI subset, or both.

evidence.text: The protocol states an ITT approach and enrolls before the discharge diagnosis is known.
The SAP defines its study population as EMS-transported adults subsequently diagnosed with MI at discharge.

requirement: Define the treatment effect and treatment attribution for participants with unsuccessful blood sampling, unavailable or delayed hs-TnI results, protocol deviations, withdrawal after randomization, non-MI discharge diagnoses, transfer, death before PCI and no PCI; preserve randomized assignment for the primary treatment-policy analysis unless another estimand is justified.

evidence.text: The protocol anticipates unsuccessful sampling or incomplete data, states ITT intent and describes withdrawal, but does not give an intercurrent-event strategy.

requirement: Before finalization, reconcile the primary endpoint wording across the sources: protocol FMC-to-PCI, SAP endpoint section and registry FMC-to-vascular-access, and SAP inferential section FMC-to-balloon; choose one event, time origin and analysis window and explain whether arterial access or balloon/device time is authoritative.

evidence.text: The protocol calls the endpoint time from FMC to PCI.
The SAP calls the endpoint FMC-to-vascular-access but later describes FMC-to-balloon and FMC-to-PCI.

requirement: Once the primary endpoint is reconciled, derive FMC from the EMS-recorded ambulance arrival time and vascular access from the timestamped arterial-access field in Swedeheart, documenting units, invalid chronology rules and cross-source linkage.

evidence.text: The reference defines FMC from the EMS record and arterial access from Swedeheart.

requirement: Prespecify an executable randomized-group primary analysis appropriate to the reconciled time outcome, including the effect measure and treatment contrast; do not use the reference SAP's modified-Poisson risk ratio for an unthresholded time in minutes, and explain whether a continuous-time model, a time-to-event model with no-PCI censoring/competing-event rules, or both is primary.
acceptable_values: censoring or competing-event rule if time-to-event

evidence.text: The reference proposes a modified-Poisson RR plus Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression for a time-in-minutes endpoint without defining a binary threshold or no-PCI handling.

requirement: For the primary comparison, report arm-specific summaries, a clearly directed treatment-effect estimate and a two-sided 95% confidence interval, not only a p-value or separate within-arm regressions.

evidence.text: The SAP names several models and says RRs and 95% CIs will be presented but does not fully specify the primary randomized contrast.

requirement: Include secondary time and utilization outcomes for FMC-to-initial-ECG, FMC-to-emergency-department admission, emergency-department length of stay and total hospital length of stay, using the stated prehospital, index-visit and up-to-14-day windows.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the secondary time and length-of-stay outcomes and windows.

requirement: Before finalization, reconcile the MACE composite: the protocol includes MI, angina, new-onset HFrEF, stroke and all-cause death, whereas the SAP definition replaces angina with PCI/CABG revascularization; define component algorithms and assess MACE separately at 72 hours and 30 days.

evidence.text: The protocol lists angina among five MACE components.
The SAP outcome list repeats angina, while its formal derivation instead lists PCI/CABG revascularization.

requirement: Compare randomized arms for MACE at 72 hours and 30 days using a binary-outcome model that reports risk ratios with robust variance and 95% confidence intervals.
acceptable_values: modified Poisson or valid log-link alternative

evidence.text: The reference assigns risk-ratio analyses to MACE at 72 hours and 30 days.

requirement: Summarize the number and types of acute-care interventions from FMC through discharge and the participant's highest level of hospital care, by randomized arm, without treating repeated interventions within one participant as independent participants.

evidence.text: The protocol defines intervention and level-of-care secondary outcomes.
The SAP expands the intervention types and hospital-care categories.

requirement: Before finalization, define one between-arm method for each length-of-stay outcome, including its distributional handling and effect measure; do not describe separate within-arm linear regressions as the treatment-effect comparison.
acceptable_values: ED and hospital length of stay

evidence.text: The reference says LOS will be analyzed separately for each arm with linear regression, which does not fully define a randomized treatment contrast.

requirement: Evaluate prehospital hs-TnI diagnostic accuracy for discharge-confirmed myocardial infarction using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value with the discharge ICD diagnosis as reference standard, and report the number of evaluable participants and confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The protocol requires sensitivity, specificity, NPV and PPV for early MI identification.
The SAP defines discharge ICD diagnosis as the reference standard.

requirement: Before finalization, resolve whether non-MI time-critical diagnoses are assessed within 72 hours, within 30 days, or at both times, and distinguish the randomized-arm treatment comparison from the descriptive positive-versus-negative hs-TnI comparison within the intervention arm.

evidence.text: The protocol states within 30 days and focuses on positive versus negative results in the intervention arm.
The SAP alternates between 72-hour and 30-day wording.

requirement: Conduct prespecified subgroup or interaction analyses for age, sex, Clinical Frailty Scale, comorbidity profile and symptom-onset interval, using the symptom-onset categories at most 120, 121-179 and at least 180 minutes for diagnostic accuracy, and label these analyses exploratory unless a confirmatory hierarchy is specified.

evidence.text: The reference lists covariate adjustment, stratified analyses and the three symptom-onset categories.

requirement: Implement the reference plan's missing-at-random multiple imputation by chained equations using type-appropriate conditional models, assess convergence and plausibility, analyze each imputed data set and combine estimates with Rubin's rules.

evidence.text: The reference specifies MAR, MICE, diagnostics and Rubin pooling.

requirement: Before finalization, specify outcome-specific missing-data and censoring rules, the imputation variables and number of imputations, and how no PCI, death before PCI, missing timestamps, failed hs-TnI tests and incomplete intervention records enter each analysis; include complete-case versus imputed and at least one plausible non-MAR sensitivity analysis.

evidence.text: The SAP gives generic MICE and complete-case sensitivity language but not outcome-specific rules or a non-MAR analysis.

requirement: State the prospective sample-size target of 1,419 participants allocated 946:473, based on 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05, an assumed 50% improvement in MI identification and a 10% allowance for unsuccessful sampling or incomplete data, while flagging that the protocol does not provide the underlying control rate or precise effect-scale calculation.

evidence.text: The protocol reports the sample-size assumptions and allocation totals but no control rate or reproducible formula.

requirement: Before finalization, define the confirmatory primary success rule and two-sided type-I-error plan, and either control multiplicity or label analyses exploratory across MACE times, length-of-stay measures, interventions, levels of care, diagnostic metrics, non-MI diagnoses and subgroup analyses.

evidence.text: The protocol lists numerous outcomes and subgroup analyses.
The SAP gives no explicit primary success criterion or multiplicity procedure.

requirement: Before the interim review after 150 participants, define its data cut, reviewing independent researchers, access to treatment assignments, safety and length-of-stay monitoring summaries, decision thresholds and authority; state that it is for validity, adherence and unforeseen-risk monitoring unless a formal efficacy/futility rule with type-I-error control is added.
acceptable_values: no efficacy claim unless alpha controlled

evidence.text: The protocol schedules external review after 150 participants and gives the PI discontinuation authority but no quantitative rule.

requirement: Before finalization, define safety summaries and the safety population for blood-sampling complications, diagnostic or treatment delay, MACE, other unforeseen risks and incidents, including arm-level event counts, participant incidences, observation windows, seriousness and relatedness; connect interim stopping to a prespecified clinically important increase in treatment time or risk.

evidence.text: The protocol discusses sampling risk, interim safety review, treatment-time monitoring and incident reporting but supplies no analysis population or tabulation plan.
